action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

The board is almost completely empty, with only a single 'x' piece at the bottom of the center column (column 3, row 5). In Connect X, the center columns provide the highest potential for vertical, horizontal, and diagonal wins, so controlling column 3 is critical. Placing an 'o' in column 3 (at row 4) directly occupies the center column, preventing the opponent from immediately stacking a second consecutive 'x' there on their next turn. This maintains balance, sets up potential 4-in-a-row threats in multiple directions as the game progresses, and follows optimal early-game strategy for the second player in an otherwise symmetric position. Other columns (such as 2 or 4) would allow the opponent to claim the center uncontested.

Playing in column 2 (or symmetrically column 4) places an x at row 5, column 2, creating a horizontal two-in-a-row with the existing x at row 5, column 3. This sets up a fork: the opponent can block at most one extension to a three-in-a-row (either column 1 or column 4 at row 5), allowing a response that forces three x's horizontally regardless of the opponent's move. Other columns do not create this forcing sequence (e.g., column 3 stacks uselessly without forming a two-in-a-row; distant columns like 1 or 5 do not adjoin the existing x). Columns 2 and 4 are equivalent by symmetry; column 2 is selected as the left optimal.

action.thoughts:
The current board has very few pieces placed (only one 'o' at row 4/column 3, plus two 'x' pieces at the bottom of columns 2 and 3). No immediate win or forced threat exists for either player. The optimal strategy at this early stage is to build rapidly toward a 4-in-a-row threat while controlling the center column.

Placing in column 3 drops to row 3 (directly above the existing 'o'), creating two vertically connected 'o' pieces in the center. From here, one additional move in the same column creates three-in-a-row (forcing the opponent to respond in that column or lose). This is the fastest path to a threat because:
- It requires no preparatory moves in other columns.
- Column 3 has the most open space above the current pieces (rows 0–2).
- The center column maximizes flexibility for future horizontal, vertical, and diagonal extensions.

Alternative placements are inferior:
- Column 2 creates a horizontal pair at row 4 but requires multiple extra moves to fill bottoms in adjacent columns before a horizontal threat can form.
- Column 4 (or others) creates only a weak diagonal connection and is even slower to develop into a threat.
- Non-connecting moves (e.g., columns 0, 1, 5, or 6) leave the existing 'o' isolated and cede the center.

This move follows standard Connect Four principles: prioritize center control and the shortest path to forcing opponent responses.

Final Answer: 3
